title: New Hire Impact Pathways and Manager Templates (2025)
body:
> **Archived 2026-03-15:** this page is superseded by "New Hire Impact Pathways and Manager Templates" and is kept for reference only.

Overview:

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's "impact-first" model for integrating new hires. It pairs a hiring intake checklist with a manager-led onboarding curriculum and a set of evaluation templates focused on early, measurable contribution, while still protecting learning time and psychological safety. The aim is a shorter time-to-impact without hurting retention or technical quality.

When to use this document:
- Managers opening new or backfill roles (IC or manager).
- People-ops partners setting up role activation gates.
- Hiring panels that need a shared readiness rubric.

Key principles:
- Task-first learning: new hires show value through small, scoped deliverables rather than extended shadowing.
- Role activation gates: binary checkpoints at 30/60/90 days backed by observable evidence.
- Manager enablement: templates and a cadence guide so integration runs predictably.
- Cross-functional alignment: map stakeholders early to clear blockers.

1) Hiring intake and role definition (before offer)

Objective: every hire has a concrete first-90-day success plan reflected in the job description and the interview loop.

Checklist (hiring manager + people-ops):
1. Write down three concrete impact deliverables for the first 90 days (e.g., add a telemetry hook to a model endpoint, finish the infra repo onboarding cert, document a cross-team integration).
2. Build a candidate assessment matrix (skills, culture add, ramp potential) with weightings (see below).
3. Name an onboarding sponsor (peer buddy) and a 30/60/90 owner (normally the manager).
4. Block dedicated onboarding time on the calendar (1 hour/day for the first week).
5. Pre-provision accounts and file the access request for SSO, repos, Slack channels and cloud tenants.

Sample candidate assessment matrix (weights):
- Core role skills: 50%
- System/product understanding: 20%
- Collaboration & communication: 15%
- Learning velocity / problem-solving: 10%
- Cultural fit & values: 5%

Interview guidance: each stage should include at least one exercise linked to a real 90-day deliverable (a design sketch or small code review for ICs, a prioritization memo for PMs). Panels record evidence against the matrix.

2) Preboarding (offer -> first day)

Owner: people-ops + hiring manager
Timeline: offer signed -> day 0

Actions:
- Send the preboarding packet including a one-page "first-week goals" summary.
- Introduce the team's 90-day deliverables and the onboarding mentor.
- Make sure the following access is in place 48-72 hours before start:

Access provisioning table:
| Access | Owner | Required by | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| SSO (Okta) | IT Ops | 72h | Primary team group assignment |
| GitHub team | Repo owner | 48h | Infra and service repos, write where needed |
| Cloud project | Cloud infra | 72h | Least privilege; escalate for elevated tasks |
| Confluence | People Ops | 48h | Edit rights on onboarding docs |
| Slack channels | Hiring manager | 24h | #team, plus #oncall if relevant |

3) First-week plan (days 0-7):

Goals: remove friction, build context, land a first tiny win.

Manager checklist:
- Day 0: Welcome and orientation (1 hour), passkeys/KMS intro, calendar and logistics.
- Day 1: Team kickoff and product context (2 hours); assign the first tiny win (e.g., reproduce a perf benchmark).
- Day 2-3: Dev environment setup with the buddy (pairing).
- Day 4: Small scoped PR or doc assigned and merged.
- Day 5: First-week retro with the manager (30 min) to surface blockers and agree a learning plan.

Manager templates:
- Welcome email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — Week 0 Plan and Resources"
- Welcome email body:
"Hi [Name], welcome aboard! Your Week 0 playbook is attached: setup steps, access links, and a first tiny win. Your buddy is [Buddy Name]. I'll check in daily during your first two weeks. — Maya"

4) 30/60/90 day activation gates

For each gate the manager collects 3 artifacts showing readiness: merged PR, architecture note, stakeholder sign-off, production telemetry, or recorded demo.

30-day gate (onboarding-enabled):
- Evidence: working dev environment; merged tiny-win PR; onboarding checklist complete.
- Pass criteria: runs core dev workflows with <4 escalations/week; follows basic code/docs standards.

60-day gate (contributing independently):
- Evidence: small feature or bugfix shipped end-to-end; led one team sync; documented a cross-team integration requirement.
- Pass criteria: owns at least one backlog item from design to deploy with manager oversight; gives clear status updates.

90-day gate (impact and ownership):
- Evidence: primary owner of a deliverable affecting customers or internal metrics; presented a runbook or postmortem; measurable metric improvement.
- Pass criteria: works independently on scoped work, gets positive peer feedback, and can onboard someone else to part of their area.

5) Manager toolkit: cadences

Minimum cadences:
- Daily quick sync (first 14 days): 10-15 min
- Weekly 1:1 with structured agenda
- 30/60/90 gate reviews (30-60 min): manager + buddy, people-ops optional

Weekly 1:1 template (30 min):
1. Status (3 min): wins and blockers
2. Weekly focus (10 min)
3. Growth and feedback (10 min)
4. Admin and actions (7 min)

First-90-day rubric (for calibration):
- Contribution velocity: Exceeds / Meets / Below
- Code quality & review behavior: Exceeds / Meets / Below
- Cross-team collaboration: Exceeds / Meets / Below
- Learning & autonomy: Exceeds / Meets / Below

6) Feedback and calibration

- At 90 days the manager sends people-ops a short "90-day readiness memo": context, evidence (3 artifacts), recommendation (pass, extend mentoring, role change).
- Quarterly calibration: hiring managers join a 90-minute forum each quarter to review a sample of memos for consistency, using an anonymized calibration sheet from people-ops.

Template: 90-day readiness memo
Subject: "90-day readiness: [Name] — [Role]"
Body: Context (2-3 lines); Evidence (artifact links); Recommendation: Pass / Extend (30 days) / Role adjustment, with rationale.

7) Escalation and extension protocol

1. Manager documents gaps and proposes a 30-day extension with explicit milestones.
2. People-ops approves the extension and any extra resources.
3. Gate review is repeated at the end of the extension.
4. If gaps remain, HR escalation for a PIP follows HR policy.

8) Snippets

Stakeholder FYI:
"Hi team — [New Hire Name] is onboarding this sprint and will own [deliverable]. Expect review requests around [date]."

Peer feedback prompt:
"Please share 3 short observations about [Name]: what went well, one thing to improve, readiness rating (1-5)."

9) Program KPIs

- Median days to pass the 90-day gate
- New-hire attrition at 6 months
- Manager satisfaction with onboarding (pulse score)
- Share of hires passing the 90-day gate without extension

Data sources: HRIS, GitHub activity, Confluence links, onboarding surveys.

Appendix A — Example first tiny wins
- Backend engineer: add metrics to a model-serving endpoint plus a dashboard tile.
- Research engineer: run the standard eval harness on a new model variant and summarize.
- Product manager: write acceptance criteria for a telemetry feature.
- Support engineer: troubleshooting runbook for the top two customer issues.
